title: Teams and Microsoft 365 admin centres: unified agent and app availability across Teams, Outlook and Microsoft 365 Copilot
summary: The briefing's rollout distinctions, administrator roles, availability controls and licensing statements are supported. Two minor corrections remain: cite the custom-app PowerShell reference and remove the catalogue-export checklist step, which has no corresponding controls row.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Microsoft plans unified agent and app availability across Teams, Outlook and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: With this change, app and agent availability  will be unified across Teams, Outlook and Microsoft 365 copilot.

claims.claim: Before this update, Integrated Apps changes in the Microsoft 365 admin center affected these apps only in Outlook and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: Before this update, changes made through the Integrated Apps section in the Microsoft 365 admin center would only affect these apps on Outlook and the Microsoft 365 copilot

claims.claim: Before this update, changes in the Teams admin center affected only Teams.
claims.quote: similarly, changes made in the Teams admin center would exclusively affect Teams.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: After unification, org-wide settings synchronise between the two admin centres.
claims.quote: After your tenant is unified, all changes to org-wide settings, agent app, status, or availability in TAC are automatically synchronized in MAC and vice versa.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: After unification, agent and app status changes synchronise between the two admin centres.
claims.quote: After unification, changes made to the app status, org-wide settings, and user assignment in either admin center are synchronized in the other.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: After unification, availability changes in either admin centre synchronise to the other.
claims.quote: Ensures consistent and synchronized agent and app behavior across platforms, as changes to app availability settings in one admin center are automatically synced with the other

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2025-11-13T00:15:06.
MC796790 associates roadmap items 393931, 485712 and 503105 with the change.
claims.quote: This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931, 485712 and 503105.

claims.claim: Phase 1 began rolling out at the end of September 2025.
claims.quote: App and agent availability unification (Section A): Rollout began in late September 2025.

claims.claim: Phase 1 targets tenants that never modified org-wide defaults, app availability or block/unblock settings in either admin centre.
claims.quote: This initial phase targets tenants that have never modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock in either the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Learn says tenants with unchanged defaults, availability and block settings are unified automatically.
claims.quote: If your tenant never modified its org-wide defaults, app availability, or app block or unblock settings in either TAC or MAC, then your tenant's app availability policies are automatically unified.

claims.claim: Phase 2 targets tenants that previously modified those settings.
claims.quote: This phase targets tenants that have previously modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock settings in either admin center.

claims.claim: MC796790 says Phase 2 is fully rolled out.
claims.quote: This phase has been fully rolled out to all tenants.

claims.claim: Modified tenants can choose to align through the Teams admin center wizard.
claims.quote: Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The modified-tenant Phase 2 experience is admin-opt-in: it changes no org-wide or app-level settings without administrator action.
claims.quote: Note: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Phase 3 will automatically unify availability for tenants that have not acted.
claims.quote: Tenants that have not taken action to unify availability through the wizard experience released in Phase 1 and Phase 2 will have their availability automatically unified across MAC and TAC as part of this phase.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft says it will announce Phase 3 timelines and details at least 60 days before that phase begins.
claims.quote: We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The supplied notice gives no Phase 3 start date.
claims.quote: The Phase 3 timeline will be announced separately, at least 60 days before that phase begins.

claims.claim: The supplied notice does not specify how Phase 3 resolves differences between admin centres.
claims.quote: We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

claims.claim: The notice's text identifies its update as 18 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 18, 2026: Unified app and agent installation management is now generally available.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Installation management is unified within 24 to 48 hours after availability unification.
claims.quote: app and agent installations are also unified across the Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC) and Teams admin center (TAC) within 24–48 hours of completing availability unification.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Installations previously made through Teams app setup policies are not unified by this change.
claims.quote: Important: App installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies. Installations previously made through those policies are not unified as part of this change.

claims.claim: Modified tenants without availability differences give consent to move to unified management.
claims.quote: Select Move to unified app management. A dialog box appears to ask for your consent to move to the unified agent and app management experience.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Tenants with differences first choose org-wide settings to apply across both admin centres.
claims.quote: The Align org-wide app settings page appears. Here you can select the org-wide default settings that you want to apply across TAC and MAC.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The wizard lets administrators resolve app status and availability differences individually by choosing an admin centre's settings.
claims.quote: Select any individual app and review the App status and Availability. Go to Review settings for the selected app to check the App status and Availability. Select the admin center’s settings that you want to apply from the Apply settings from drop-down list and select Apply settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The wizard also lets administrators resolve app differences in bulk.
claims.quote: Bulk app resolution: Select multiple apps at a time and select either Teams admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center from the Apply settings from drop-down list.

claims.claim: The wizard can download app status and availability comparison settings as CSV.
claims.quote: Download the CSV file: Select the Excel icon in the top-right corner to download the App status and Availability settings as a CSV file.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Any Teams or Global admin can prepare updates through the Review summary page.
claims.quote: Any Teams or Global admin can make updates upto the Review summary page.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Only a Global admin can consent and apply the final unification changes.
claims.quote: Only a Global admin can give consent and apply the final changes.

claims.claim: Learn's unified management page points readers to roadmap item 485712 for timelines.
claims.quote: For timelines, see Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 485712.

claims.claim: Learn lists avoiding mismatched configurations as a purpose of unification.
claims.quote: Avoids mismatched configurations

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The roadmap describes availability management rather than new data access or new agent actions.
claims.quote: Administrators using the Microsoft 365 admin center and Teams admin center who manage agents and apps that work across Teams, Outlook and the Microsoft 365 copilot will be able to apply their changes consistently across all these surfaces.

claims.claim: A single org-wide third-party control manages bulk availability for new and existing third-party agents and apps.
claims.quote: Under Third-party apps, a single control manages the bulk availability of both the new and existing third-party agents and apps.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Availability changes take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect.

claims.claim: In rare cases availability changes take up to six days to appear in the client.
claims.quote: In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Each user requires a Teams licence to use Teams, except for joining meetings anonymously.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included under the product-level Teams licence requirement, rather than a documented unification-specific entitlement.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence specific to availability unification is published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams unified agent app management license unification pricing; unified app management licensing pricing license meter. Read learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/uam-tac-mac, /user-access and /purchase-third-party-apps; no unification-specific licence stated.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Learn names Teams Administrator as the role needed to use the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks

claims.claim: The cited management and licensing pages document no meter or charge for unification itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams unified agent app management license unification pricing; unified app management licensing pricing license meter. Read Learn uam-tac-mac, manage-apps, user-access and purchase-third-party-apps; no unification meter or charge stated.

claims.claim: Some paid Teams apps require separate service subscriptions for their functionality.
claims.quote: Some Teams apps require purchasing a service subscription to use app functionality. These service subscriptions are called Software as a Service (SaaS) offers.

claims.claim: Administrators can view and manage only agents and apps deployed in the same release channel as their tenant.
claims.quote: You can only view and manage agents and apps that are deployed in the same release channel as your tenant is.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center can export the organisation's agent and app catalogue as CSV for checking status and availability.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can export the entire agent and app catalog for your org from the Teams admin center. It can help you to coordinate with admin and security teams to evaluate agents and apps, verify availability, verify status, and more.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Move to unified app management opens the tenant unification experience.
claims.quote: Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. Select Move to unified app management. A dialog box appears to ask for your consent to move to the unified agent and app management experience.

claims.claim: No cmdlet or API is documented for running the move-to-unified-management wizard.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Move to unified app management Microsoft Graph API PowerShell migration; unified app management PowerShell migration wizard API. Read Learn uam-tac-mac, Update-M365TeamsApp and Graph teamsAppSettings beta; no migration operation found.

claims.claim: The printed Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability > Available to path reaches per-app availability.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. Select Edit availability. Select the required option from Available to menu.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone sets app availability to everyone.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone
Updates the availability value for Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b) to Everyone.

claims.claim: AppAssignmentType accepts Everyone, UsersAndGroups and Noone.
claims.quote:
-AppAssignmentType
App availability type.
Parameter sets
(Everyone
UsersandGroups
Noone)

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block controls the app's organisation-wide status.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked $true is a documented app-state operation.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: The reference describes IsBlocked as app state but labels its $true example as unblocking.
claims.quote:
-IsBlocked
The state of the app in the tenant.
Example 3
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > app type > Let users install and use available apps by default reaches the org-wide availability defaults.
claims.quote: On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. You can then configure the settings in the pane. Under Custom apps, turn off or turn on Let users install and use available apps by default option.

claims.claim: No automation for the org-wide availability defaults was found as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph Teams org-wide app settings default availability PowerShell API. Read Learn app-centric-management, Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp and Graph teamsAppSettings/customAppSettings beta; no availability-default operation found.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp controls custom-app uploading rather than the availability default.
claims.quote: If the isSideloadedAppsInteractionEnabled is set to true, the switch is enabled. So that the custom apps can be uploaded as app packages and available in the organization's app store, vice versa.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamssettingscustomapp?view=teams-ps to sources with title 'Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp'; this reference supports the distinction in controls[3].note.

claims.claim: Org-wide app setting changes take effect after a few hours.
claims.quote: Select Save. The settings take effect after a few hours.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Org-wide availability defaults do not override individually saved app availability assignments.
claims.quote: Your change to the org-wide app setting applies only to those apps for which you didn't change the availability.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp belongs to MicrosoftTeams and updates app state, availability and installation.
claims.quote:
Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module
This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference does not state whether its changes synchronise with the Microsoft 365 admin center in unified tenants.
claims.quote: Searched: Update-M365TeamsApp unified management synchronize Microsoft 365 admin center. Read the complete Update-M365TeamsApp reference and uam-tac-mac; the cmdlet reference has no unification or cross-admin-centre synchronisation statement.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, catalogue-export bullet
claims.claim: The governance checklist's catalogue-export instruction has no corresponding control row.
claims.quote: Export the agent and app catalogue from the Teams admin center as CSV. Controls cover moving to unified management, per-app availability, allow/block status and org-wide defaults, but not catalogue export.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet beginning 'Export the agent and app catalogue from the Teams admin center as CSV'; it asks readers to use a control not represented in the controls table.
